question: The Recorder’s Court was later replaced by the ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Recorder's Court in India was replaced by the **Supreme Court** under the provisions of the Regulating Act of 1773.
 
• The Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (Calcutta) was established in **1774** as the first Supreme Court in British India.
 
• The establishment of the Supreme Court aimed to introduce a unified judicial system in British-controlled territories.
 
• The Supreme Court had original, appellate, and admiralty jurisdiction and was intended to administer justice based on English law.
 
• The court replaced the Recorder's Court, which was earlier functioning in some British settlements in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Recorder's Court**

 
 
• The Recorder's Court was a type of court established by the British in colonial territories to handle legal matters.
 
• It was primarily tasked with adjudicating civil and criminal cases in British-controlled areas.
 
• The Recorder's Court was presided over by a judge known as the "Recorder."
 
 
 
• **Regulating Act of 1773**
 
 
• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first attempt by the British government to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• It established the Supreme Court at Calcutta and marked the beginning of a centralized judicial system in India.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William**
 
 
• It was the first Supreme Court in India and was established in Calcutta in 1774.
 
• The court had jurisdiction over Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
• It consisted of a Chief Justice and three other judges.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Evolution in British India**
 
 
• The judicial system evolved over time, with the creation of High Courts in 1862 and the abolition of the Supreme Court under the Indian High Courts Act of 1861.
 
• These High Courts eventually became the foundation of the Indian judicial system.
